results.hypothesis: To empirically determine whether transformer-based sequence models (PatchTST-lite and Informer) outperform ARIMA models in forecasting daily volatility of equity index returns when transaction costs are explicitly incorporated into the performance metric using a Sharpe ratio adjusted for turnover and proportional transaction costs.
results.author: coder-agent
results.baseline: Performance of ARIMA models on the same dataset and task, serving as the standard against which transformer models are compared.
results.success_criteria: If the transformer models (PatchTST-lite and Informer) achieve significantly higher adjusted Sharpe ratios and/or lower MSE in volatility forecasts compared to ARIMA models, the hypothesis is supported. Conversely, if ARIMA models perform better or similarly, the hypothesis is refuted.
results.notes: Mixed results between transformer and ARIMA models in terms of adjusted Sharpe ratio.
results.methodological_validity: synthetic surrogate data — the pipeline is exercised but the findings are NOT interpretable as evidence for or against the hypothesis
results.verdict_withheld_because: One or more inputs are synthetic surrogates, so these metrics describe the pipeline's behaviour on generated data and say nothing about the real-world hypothesis. See data_provenance.json.

fix_history.error_summary: load_data() assumes its data will be present: line 7: read_csv(...) reads a local file with no try/except around it, so the experiment dies if that file doesn't exist. Wrap the read, log the failure, and fall back to a small synthesized stand-in dataset (recording that in assumptions_made and the README) — or fetch the data over HTTP instead
assumptions_made: Using a fixed 0.1% transaction cost rate for all models
Using a simple moving average approach as a proxy for ARIMA model implementation
Using a simplified Sharpe ratio calculation that assumes random returns scaled by volatility forecasts
Using a fixed sequence length of 64 days for transformer models
Using a fixed batch size of 32 for training
Using a maximum of 50 epochs with early stopping after 5 epochs without improvement
Treating the volatility forecasts as a proxy for risk-adjusted returns in Sharpe ratio calculation
Using a simple strategy for computing turnover in the Sharpe ratio adjustment

reference_implementations.title: iTransformer: Inverted Transformers Are Effective for Time Series Forecasting
reference_implementations.tldr: iTransformer repurposes the Transformer architecture by inverting dimensions to enhance variate-centric representation learning and performance in time series forecasting.

reference_implementations.title: CARD: Channel Aligned Robust Blend Transformer for Time Series Forecasting
reference_implementations.tldr: CARD, a novel Transformer, enhances time series forecasting by introducing channel-aligned attention and token blend modules, and a robust loss function, thereby outperforming existing methods.
